purpose: Provide an audit-ready, standards-anchored register of sustainability-related metrics and targets, enabling users to assess performance, progress against targets, and the robustness of measurement (scope, boundary, methodology, and assurance status).
tone: Formal, standards-led, compliance-oriented, and decision-useful. Objective and non-promotional. Forward-looking only where bounded (planned enhancements stated with clear limitations and dependencies). Explicit about uncertainty, data maturity, and comparability constraints.
level_of_detail: High traceability and definitional detail. Narrative is concise and primarily frames the tables; technical depth is provided through structured definitions, scoping notes, reconciliation blocks, and methodology summaries (with pointers to fuller methodology elsewhere when needed).
paragraph_style: Start with a brief navigational overview of subsections, then a short rationale tied to disclosure requirements. Use short bridging paragraphs to explain metric selection, target linkage, and how to read the tables. Use compact bullet lists for inclusion/exclusion criteria and calculation steps. Keep narrative subordinate to the metric register.
sentence_style: Precise, declarative, and bounded. Prefer requirement-based phrasing and clear qualifiers (scope, boundary, period, coverage). Avoid superlatives. Use consistent terminology for metrics, targets, boundaries, and assurance.
preferred_evidence_style: Centralize evidence in a metric register table that combines definition, value/status, provenance (external standard reference and internal source), and mapping to report pillars. Use footnotes for technical conventions and assurance notes. Where complex, add a reconciliation block (eligible population to reported subset) and a short calculation approach summary with stepwise logic.
table_usage: Primary vehicle for disclosure. Use a consistent column set across pages and repeat headers for multi-page tables. Allow mixed quantitative and qualitative entries (including status placeholders for unavailable data). Include units in headers, right-align numeric columns, and use consistent formatting. Add optional secondary tables for disaggregation (by category) and reconciliation (gross to scoped).
figure_usage: Optional and only when it materially improves comprehension (e.g., distribution by category, scoping waterfall). If figures are used, keep narrative references brief and ensure captions mirror metric name and segmentation basis. Do not replace traceability fields with visuals; tables remain the authoritative record.
how_to_discuss_missing_data: Use explicit, neutral placeholders (e.g., not available for the reporting period; not included; not applicable) and state the reason category (data availability, boundary decision, methodology not yet implemented). Indicate planned enhancements as intentions with dependencies (systems, data providers, methodological development) without overpromising. Preserve completeness by listing the metric even when not reported.
what_to_avoid: Company-specific names, internal document titles, URLs, contact details, or proprietary process descriptions
Any numeric values, percentages, totals, time horizons, or quantified achievements embedded in narrative examples
Promotional or leadership claims (e.g., best-in-class, industry-leading) or implied effectiveness without evidence
Jurisdiction-specific regulatory statements presented as universally applicable facts; reference regulation only as a general pattern where applicable
Exact copied wording from standards, assurance statements, or formulas; paraphrase and keep generic
Overly long storytelling paragraphs that duplicate what tables already show
Unqualified forward-looking commitments; avoid certainty where data maturity is limited
